ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, individuals with significant control, authorized agents, and any corporate UBO against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and non-SDN lists; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) Canadian sanctions regulations enacted under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act, including Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list; (iv) Her Majesty's Treasury/OFsi sanctions list for entities using UK/EU payment corridors; and (v) applicable domestic PEP databases and regulatory enforcement lists. For Canadian AML/CFT purposes, regulated service providers must apply FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons and beneficial ownership, perform reasonable measures to verify identity and authority of signatories, and retain all CDD/KYC records for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Services / BC Corporate Registry (Corporate Online) via bcregistry.gov.bc.ca and corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC business corporation may adopt a name in English, French, or a combined form, using Latin-alphabet characters transliterated into English/French if the original script is non-Latin. The corporate name must contain a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., Limited, Incorporated, or Corporation, or must be a numbered company. The name must not be confusingly similar to an existing name, trademark, or reserved name, and must not misappropriate a regulated term unless prior consent or ministerial approval is obtained. Registry practice requires proposed names to be distinctive and not merely descriptive of the business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: BC name reservations cannot be extended; if a name request is rejected or expires, a new name request with revised distinctive elements must be filed. Upon rejection, the applicant may write to the BC Corporate Registry seeking written reasons and reconsideration, attaching any consents or evidence that cure the stated grounds. If the Registrar of Companies upholds the rejection, the applicant may file a further administrative reconsideration notice with legal argument and then may apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, if the refusal is based on an error of law or an unreasonable exercise of discretion. In practice, the most efficient remedy is resubmission of a similar but sufficiently distinctive name together with any required regulatory consent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A BC business corporation must maintain a registered office and a records office in British Columbia. A mailbox-only virtual address does not satisfy the statutory requirement. A virtual office provided by a licensed BC corporate services agent that maintains a physical street address in BC, has personnel able to receive service of process, and provides registered-office and records-office services is generally accepted by the BC Registry. For the AI/LLM API platform, a virtual office is permissible for corporate registration purposes, but it does not create Canadian tax residence or commercial substance; Canada Revenue Agency will look to central management and control, board meetings, personnel, and substantive business activities when determining tax residence and whether the entity has a permanent establishment in BC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: 8% during the first year. The BC Registrar does not routinely conduct unannounced physical inspections of private business corporations. CRA inspections and audits are normally preceded by notice. FINTRAC AML/CFT examinations would arise only if the company later becomes a money services business or a reporting entity under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, which is not the intended scope for a pure AI/LLM API platform. Most physical-verification pressure will come from regulated banking and payment partners undertaking KYB and KYC checks rather than from statutory government inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 1, 10, 12, 14, 91, 98, 113, 184, 188 and 210
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) filed online through BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. The initial share capital may be issued for such consideration as the subscribers determine; shares may be with or without par value.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation’s corporate existence be confirmed, and the registered office at [Street, City, British Columbia] be approved with the Registrar of Companies as its address for process service. RESOLVED that the subscription agreement be accepted, and the subscribers are authorized to acquire [number] Class A Common Shares for agreed fair consideration, which shares shall be deemed fully paid. RESOLVED that the proposed by-laws be adopted, and the following officers be appointed: President [name], Secretary [name], and Treasurer [name]. The officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute banking instructions, and approve routine corporate expenses. All material operational and financial decisions remain reserved to the Board. step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online, BC Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search selecting a distinct English and Chinese corporate name, include the required legal element 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', or 'Limited', and submit the Name Reservation Request online with valid director names and contact details.
required_dossiers: Identity and contact details of applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or the reserved name expires, submit an amendment to the registration or file a fresh name reservation request with alternative names and await re-assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry via BC Corporate Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles by specifying authorized share structure, first directors, registered office address, and records office. Submit electronically and pay the filing fee using credit card or deposit account.
required_dossiers: Consent of named directors to act
Primary and alternate registered office address details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or flagged for correction, revise and resubmit electronically within 30 days of notification, curing any signature, share structure, or registered office deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Certificate of Incorporation and the endorsed Notice of Articles once the application is approved. Verify the corporate name, BC company number, and effective incorporation date, and retain these documents in the corporate records book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, submit a Request for Correction in Writing to the Registrar of Companies, attaching supporting documents and statutory confirmation for administrative correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening and Recording First Directors' Board Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, adopt the approved by-laws, appoint officers, approve share issuance, open bank accounts, and authorize issuance of share certificates. Record minutes and executed resolutions in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Minute book and share certificate stock
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Errors in meeting procedure can be cured by unanimous resolution under s. 148 of the Business Corporations Act, subject to shareholder confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office address is located in British Columbia and is not solely a post-office box. Designate a records office, which may be at the registered office, where the articles, by-laws, resolutions, register of directors, register of shareholders, and financial records are maintained.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office designation fails due to incomplete consent, provide the landlord's written acknowledgement or update registered office information through BC Corporate Online and file a corrected Notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Licence Application with Local Municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Hall / City Licensing Department in the municipality of the registered or business operations address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a general business licence and confirm that the premises are zoned to permit administrative/office use. Include identity documents, certificate of incorporation, and lease/ownership evidence. Payment of applicable licence fee is required.
required_dossiers: Government-issued ID for applicant and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning or use conditions are challenged, obtain a confirmatory zoning opinion, apply for a variance, provide evidence that only online API services are conducted at the premises, or relocate to compliant commercial premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Community Planning and Business Licensing Division, local municipal government

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Environmental Assessment Office and Metro Vancouver Waste Management / municipal sewer authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category B: administrative/technology office use producing no listed industrial discharges or emissions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, no point-source air emissions, no storage of hazardous waste. Office-generated sanitary waste must conform to municipal sewer bylaw discharge limits for BOD, suspended solids, and acceptable pH range (typically 5.5–10.0), and e-waste, batteries, and electronic equipment must be disposed through permitted scrap or recycling channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate or annual inspection per local fire code; electrical and structural load review for erecting heavy server racks, if any; compliance with WorkSafeBC Occupational Health and Safety Regulation through emergency readiness, first-aid supplies, washroom capacity, and ergonomic workstation standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); Business Registration Online portal and CRA My Business Account
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on taxable GST/HST activity in Canada must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) with an RT program account. Registration is initiated via Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number), through Business Registration Online, or by calling the CRA non-resident GST/HST registration line. The foreign entity must provide its constitutional documents, foreign tax identification number, Canadian address or authorized representative/local agent, and details of anticipated Canadian taxable supplies. CRA issues a 9-digit BN and the separate 2-letter/digit program account for GST/HST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box classification system. A business corporation is always an entity-level taxpayer subject to federal Part I tax and provincial corporate income tax. For foreign legal entities, CRA applies a domestic-law characterization test, not elective classification. Relevant statutory elections include the section 216(1) election for non-resident lessors, capital cost allowance elections, and the hybrid-mismatch rules under sections 18.2 and 18.8 which disallow excessive interest payments in cross-border arrangements and operate as an anti-avoidance election-limitation regime. No pass-through classification is available for a corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) at 7%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter, or CAD 50,000 in the last four consecutive calendar quarters of total taxable worldwide supplies after intercompany sales reduction; BC PST registration is required before making taxable retail sales in British Columbia with no general small-supplier exemption
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API digital stamping, or PEPPOL e-invoicing mandate. CRA accepts electronic invoices; GST/HST returns must be filed electronically for registrants with annual taxable turnover over CAD 1,500,000, and certain registrants must use GST/HST NETFILE. In BC, PST vendors maintain their own records but there is no fiscal clearance API requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, zero-rated exports under section 21 of the Excise Tax Act apply where the exporter satisfies CRA that the goods were delivered to a destination outside Canada and exported as part of a sale. For services, section 22 zero-rates a supply made to a non-resident person unless the supply is made to a non-resident who is registered for GST/HST or the service relates to real property or tangible personal property located in Canada. AI/LLM API platform services supplied to foreign API customers are generally zero-rated if the contract, payment, and place of use are outside Canada; the supplier must retain documentary evidence proving non-resident recipient status and off-Canada consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) for physical goods exported from Canada
Commercial invoice and non-resident service agreement demonstrating the place of supply
Bill of Lading or other shipping/carrier evidence for tangible property exports
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank payment advice, SWIFT/transfer records proving inflow of foreign currency
Technical usage logs and IP-address evidence for AI API platform services consumed outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export zero-rating claims with heightened scrutiny on AI, digital, and cross-border API arrangements. If the 0% GST/HST rate is applied incorrectly, CRA may assess uncollected GST/HST plus interest and civil penalties. Fraudulent export transactions attract gross negligence penalties up to 30% of the assessed amount, false-statement penalties, prosecution, and a general four-year reassessment window extended to ten years in cases of neglect or misrepresentation. Failure to retain required export documentation destroys the zero-rating justification and triggers immediate clawback of input tax credits and refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — monetary and financial-system authority; foreign-exchange policy operates through a free-floating regime rather than administrative controls. Currency issuance and exchange-rate framework rest on the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52). Prudential supervision of banks is delegated to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/ATF supervision is vested in the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); payments-system oversight is shared between the Bank of Canada and Payments Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility with zero exchange controls; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951. There are no restrictions on dividend remittances, interest payments, equity liquidation proceeds, or capital repatriation. Non-resident shareholders of a British Columbia corporation receiving dividends are subject to Part XIII withholding tax at a 25% statutory rate, generally reduced to 5–15% under an applicable tax treaty (e.g., Canada–US Treaty). The Canadian dollar is freely deliverable on global markets; no government approval is required for payment routing, foreign-currency account maintenance, or profit repatriation. The only administrative gate for a non-resident founder establishing a BC operating company is the Investment Canada Act notification for new Canadian business establishment, which is a filing requirement rather than an FX or capital-control approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline for export receipts. Any entity may retain USD, EUR, CNY, or other foreign-currency proceeds indefinitely in domestic or offshore accounts. Cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are subject to FINTRAC reporting (record-keeping and transmission of EFT reports), but this is a transparency measure, not a conversion or surrender obligation. No BC-specific invoicing or export-license rules apply to software/API exports.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD and USD) and Capital Escrow Account available for share-subscription funds through RBC Trust or law-firm escrow
Operational Account (CAD/USD); no dedicated capital escrow product for low-risk tech entities
Operational Account plus Cross-Border USD Banking; Capital Escrow Account available via Scotiatrust for non-resident equity injections
Operational Account with USD clearing through BMO Harris Bank; escrow capacity limited to commercial custody arrangements
Operational Account only; non-resident onboarding capacity is limited and capital escrow is unavailable
Operational Account; Quebec-centric footprint and reduced BC commercial coverage

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for payment collection and FX intermediation layers; MEDIUM as a full treasury-banking substitute. Legal constraints: (1) Canadian fintech EMIs — e.g., Wise Canada, an MSB registered with FINTRAC, and Stripe Canada as a payment facilitator — are not deposit-taking institutions; CRA payroll program accounts, Part XIII withholding settlement, and corporate tax payments must be made through a Schedule I chartered bank account; (2) if the BC entity itself accepts USDC as customer payment, it likely triggers MSB registration under the PCMLTFA's 'dealing in virtual currency' provisions unless the collection and conversion are contractually performed by a registered MSB payment processor; (3) the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) imposes registration on the payment service provider, but the merchant must demonstrate contractual and operational segregation of client funds to the Bank of Canada; (4) treasury risk limits — fintech rails should be capped below 30% of monthly FX flows to maintain banker confidence and liquidity redundancy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted; Canadian law does not require physical director appearance. Every Schedule I bank nevertheless mandates a live video-verification call with all directors and ultimate beneficial owners. Practical requirements: (a) at least one signing officer with a Canadian nexus — e.g., a Vancouver-based chief financial officer or registered agent holding a power of attorney — to execute account documents electronically; (b) FATCA/CRS declarations and a corporate-ownership waterfall; (c) non-waivable UBO video interview; (d) a BC registered-office address and, for the bank's economic-substance questionnaire, evidence of Canadian operational presence. Fully digital, no-human-touch, no-Canadian-nexus account opening is not available for a BC provincial corporation at any Tier-1 bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fintech/crypto exposure — bank flags the USDC payment rail as virtual-currency dealing and requires enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC MSB registration certificate for the entity or a contractual guarantee that receipts are swept exclusively through a registered MSB exchange; wallet-address allow-list and sanctions screening of blockchain addresses; written crypto policy; real-time transaction-monitoring logs; proof of conversion to fiat within 24–48 hours; legal opinion distinguishing USDC settlement from speculative dealing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO and thin Canadian substance — bank flags opaque ownership of a BC provincial corporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Notice of Articles, corporate-registry extract, 100% UBO waterfall with certified passport copies, notarized UBO declaration, registered-office lease, Canadian employment contracts, CRA business-number registration confirming payroll and GST/HST accounts, and a board resolution ratifying the bank as principal depository.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire velocity inconsistent with the declared AI API activity profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master API Licensing Agreements, token-metering usage reports from the platform, per-wire commercial-nexus memorandum, customer screening reports, and a monthly reconciliation between API revenue and SWIFT credits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share-capital injection raises source-of-funds concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement, board resolution authorizing share issuance, investor bank statements demonstrating legitimate fund accumulation, ISED Investment Canada Act new-business notification receipt, notarized source-of-wealth questionnaire, and Canadian tax counsel opinion on paid-up capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP matching on founder or counterparty names
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results from Canada's Special Economic Measures Act sanctions list, OFAC, EU, and UN lists; negative media and adverse-information reports; PEP self-declaration; UBO identity-resolution documentation; and a remediation letter from compliance counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Protocol: SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or MT202 COV for large same-day settlement routed to the BC operating account or a Tier-1 Capital Escrow Account. ISO 20022 purpose code: SCVE (Share Capital / Payment of Capital) with narrative 'Equity injection — Generative AI LLM API Platform, ISIC 6201'; alternatively 'FDI' where the non-resident investor treaty discloses foreign direct investment. Verification package: share-subscription agreement, board resolution, Notice of Articles, shareholder register update, ISED new-business notification, and source-of-funds bank statements. Banks apply enhanced verification for any wire from a crypto-exchange counterparty; prefer institution-to-institution transfers. Large-value CAD settlement occurs over Lynx (Bank of Canada RTSS); cross-border USD may be cleared via the corresponding US correspondent (Fedwire/CHIPS). FINTRAC records apply to all EFTs >= CAD 10,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for global supplier disbursements, cloud-infrastructure payments, and licensing fees, with purpose codes reflecting true commercial substance; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) through the bank's trade-finance desk for GPU server procurement and colocation contracts exceeding CAD 100,000; (3) Lynx RTGS for same-day CAD settlement of domestic disbursements; (4) ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System) for low-value recurring CAD payments; (5) USDC-based disbursements only through FINTRAC-registered Canadian MSB exchangers, converting immediately to CAD/USD; (6) FX conversion strategy: maintain dual-currency accounts (CAD operating + USD clearing) and a standing FX conversion line with a 25–35-basis-point margin to minimize conversion leakage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/CNY, CAD/EUR) with tenors up to 12 months via Tier-1 bank FX desk; no ISDA CSA required for plain-vanilla corporate lines
FX swaps (CAD/USD swap-in/swap-out) for short-term liquidity conversion between operating and clearing accounts
Vanilla FX options (CAD call / USD put and CAD put / USD call) permissible under bank derivative authority, subject to board-approved derivatives policy

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term balance-sheet hedging of USD-denominated convertible notes or revenue-share financings; requires ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Schedule and Credit Support Annex

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedging emerging-market API customer receipts (INR, IDR, BRL, NGN) where the underlying currency is non-deliverable; NDFs are not required for CAD, which is fully convertible and deliverable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registries and Consumer Services (Corporate Registry) of the Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If not filed within 60 days of the anniversary, the registrar may issue a strike-off notice; persistent non-compliance results in administrative dissolution. Reinstatement requires payment of outstanding fees and may require court approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's taxation year-end (for a December 31 year-end, by June 30 of the following calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or remit tax attracts a penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, a 10% repeated-failure penalty, compound daily interest, and potential director liability for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private BC business corporation has no statutory audit mandate. An audit is compulsory if the corporation is a reporting issuer under securities legislation, an offering corporation, or a regulated financial company. Private corporations may dispense with an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution; a court may order an audit on a shareholder application. No revenue or asset threshold alone triggers a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for reporting issuers and publicly accountable enterprises; private BC companies may elect to use Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Part 2.2 of the BCBCA, a relevant BC company must maintain an individual-with-significant-control (ISC) register and deliver an ISC confirmation to BC Registries with each annual report. Any change in ISC information must be recorded in the register and reported to the registry within 30 days. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members before the annual report is delivered; the Register of Directors must be updated concurrently with appointments and resignations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $150–500 USD per year for a registered office address and corporate agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000–15,000 USD if a statutory or contracted audit is triggered; otherwise nil

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general corporate rate (federal 15% + British Columbia provincial 12%); 11% combined small-business rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations (federal 9% + BC 2%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED Investment Tax Credit: 35% fully refundable for CCPCs on up to CAD 3,000,000 of qualified expenditures (15% non-refundable above the cap and for non-CCPCs); BC provincial SR&ED credit of 10% refundable on qualifying expenses; 100% immediate expense of eligible application software under CCA Class 12; Class 50 computing hardware at 55% declining balance; accelerated treatment for eligible clean-energy compute infrastructure; exported AI/LLM API services generally zero-rated for GST/HST and exempt from BC PST where the supply is an exported service

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the CRA My Business Account portal or CRA-certified tax preparation software (EFILE/T2); paper filing is restricted to limited exceptional circumstances
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual fiscal-period return; quarterly corporate income tax instalments are required where net tax owing exceeds CAD 3,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 filing due on or before six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance-due remittance due two months after the fiscal year-end (three months for eligible CCPCs claiming the small-business deduction)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporation name, Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and account identifier, fiscal period end date, jurisdiction of incorporation, tax shelter flags, and election cross-references
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Canadian Business Number and disclose the foreign residency of the ultimate parent in the ownership section; complete the foreign-affiliate schedules (Form T1134) where the foreign ownership or foreign IP holding structure exceeds the statutory cost-based thresholds

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total consideration accruing for AI/LLM API token sales, platform subscriptions, inference credits, and usage-based billing, net of GST/HST and trade discounts; accrual basis is mandatory
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue of a non-resident-owned corporation must reflect Canadian-source business profits only; do not net intercompany royalties, cloud pass-through charges, or foreign withholding against gross revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 20 – Total deductions and operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cloud hosting, GPU/compute capacity, data acquisition, developer payroll, marketing, professional fees, software licenses, and amortization of capitalized development
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every intercompany charge (model licenses, IP royalties, management fees, compute sharing) must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and reported on Form T106 when the aggregate fair market value of transactions with any one non-resident exceeds CAD 1,000,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after all deductions, capital cost allowance, loss carryovers, and statutory reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only treaty-consistent loss utilization; losses of the Canadian subsidiary cannot be surrendered to a foreign parent, and non-resident-owned investment corporations are ineligible for small-business loss streaming

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal base tax at 15%, BC provincial tax at 12%, small-business deduction on the CAD 500,000 active business limit, investment tax credits including SR&ED, and refundable dividend tax on ineligible Part IV dividends
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-CCPC and non-resident-controlled entities cannot claim the small-business deduction; verify treaty non-discrimination provisions before assuming provincial credit eligibility; claim foreign tax credits only for creditable foreign source business taxes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed operating expense breakdown for the AI/LLM API business including hosting, salaries, royalties, amortization, and bad debts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transparently segregate deductible Canadian expenditures from foreign-parent allocations; any cost-plus or TNMM charge should match the documented intercompany agreement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 3 – Depreciation and capital cost allowance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CCA computation by class: Class 12 application software at 100%, Class 50 computer hardware at 55% declining balance, Class 43.1/43.2 clean-energy equipment at accelerated rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Canadian entity must hold legal and beneficial ownership of servers and software to support CCA claims; a foreign-parent IP holding arrangement must not duplicate depreciation and royalty deductions on the same economic asset

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of non-capital loss carryovers (20 years) and net-capital loss carryovers (3 years back and indefinite forward) applied in the tax year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Demonstrate continuity of the Canadian business and ownership; acquisition of control by non-residents may trigger a deemed year-end and restrict loss utilization under the acquisition-of-control rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the CAD 500,000 small-business limit among associated Canadian corporations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian subsidiary that is controlled, directly or indirectly, by non-residents is not a CCPC and is excluded from the business limit; joint venture and partnership arrangements require special allocation schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information return covering non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents, including intercompany API licensing, royalty payments, interest, and management charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when the aggregate fair market value of covered transactions with a single non-resident exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year; file on or before the T2 due date and attach the transfer pricing methodology, functional risk analysis, and comparables

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of default up to 12 months; a second failure within three years raises the penalty to 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months. Arrears interest accrues at the CRA prescribed rate (set quarterly, compounded daily). Late or incorrect T106 reporting attracts daily penalties of CAD 100 per form per day, subject to statutory minimums and caps; late foreign-affiliate schedules (T1134) attract CAD 25 per day penalties (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per return).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; withholding is federally administered with no additional BC provincial layer
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty-reduced rates: (1) obtain an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the shareholder's resident tax authority; (2) complete CRA Form NR301 (Application for Treaty-Based Waiver of Withholding Tax) and file it, together with the TRC, with the CRA International Tax Services Office; (3) where the CRA is satisfied, it notifies the payer that reduced withholding applies, or the payer may withhold at the treaty rate on receipt of a completed NR301 and TRC. Over-withheld Part XIII tax may be recovered by the non-resident filing Form NR7-R within two years of the end of the calendar year in which tax was withheld. Under the Canada-US treaty (the dominant fact pattern): 15% portfolio dividend withholding, reduced to 5% where a US corporation beneficially owns at least 10% of the voting stock of the Canadian payer; comparable reductions exist under other comprehensive DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25% for both royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty-reduced Canada-US rates: interest 15% generally, with 0% available for certain arm's-length long-term debt; royalties 10% generally, with 0% for specific payments such as software copyright-related royalties. Many other Canadian treaties provide 10-15% royalty caps and 10-15% interest caps. Relief is available at source only after NR301 and TRC compliance, otherwise the non-resident must use NR7-R for a refund within the statutory two-year window.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory registration threshold for transfer-pricing documentation, but contemporaneous records are mandatory under ITA s.247(4) and Information Circular IC87-2R; Form T106 must be filed where the aggregate fair market value of non-arm's-length transactions with any one non-resident exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year. Country-by-country reporting applies to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 789,000,000. The s.247(3) adjustment penalty applies where the upward international transfer-pricing adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 and 10% of gross revenue.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Any other method producing an arm's-length result consistent with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines as accepted by the CRA
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not impose offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under ITA s.245 denies tax benefits from avoidance transactions lacking genuine economic substance. ITA s.247, IC87-2R, and CRA administrative policy require a documented functional and risk analysis evidencing that the Canadian entity has the people, assets, and decision-making authority to support its intercompany profits. For an AI/LLM API platform, the Canadian corporation must own the customer contracts, employ the developers and risk functions, retain pricing discretion, and pay arm's-length royalties for any foreign-resident licensed IP. A hollow Canadian cash-box that passively routes USDC/token revenue to a foreign parent while claiming SR&ED credits and treaty benefits will be recharacterized under GAAR, the sham doctrine, and transfer-pricing anti-abuse rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly making false or misleading statements in a T2 return, falsifying books and records, destroying documentation, or willfully omitting cross-border AI API revenue settled through crypto rails or foreign bank accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under ITA s.239(1): fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, imprisonment up to five years, and full restitution of evaded tax plus interest; civil gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2) equal to 25% of the understated tax, stacked on the 5%/1% late-filing penalty regime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized or participated in false filings face personal assessment under ITA s.227.1 for unremitted Part XIII withholding and source deductions notwithstanding corporate insolvency; criminal proceedings permit asset freezes, forfeiture orders, bail conditions restricting travel, and director-veil-piercing where corporate funds were diverted

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Foreign Information Return Failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing intercompany model-licensing royalties or cloud compute fees to a non-resident parent, failing to file Form T106 for non-arm's-length transactions crossing the CAD 1,000,000 threshold, or preparing no contemporaneous documentation before the filing due date
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment penalty under ITA s.247(3): 10% of the net adjustment where the adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 and 10% of gross revenue; T106 late-filing penalties of CAD 100 per day per form up to CAD 2,500, accumulating until corrected; additional 25% gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2); interest on reassessed amounts runs from the original filing due date
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically exposed for corporate transfer-pricing penalties, but personal exposure arises where they knowingly authorize false documentation, breach fiduciary duties by diverting IP value, or participate in wilful collusion with a foreign parent, triggering criminal s.239 charges and director-level restitution orders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Sham, GAAR, and AML (PCMLTFA)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Canadian corporation as a hollow conduit with no Canadian employees, premises, board activity, or substantive decision-making; passively routing USDC/token revenue through Stripe or crypto exchanges to a foreign parent; structuring solely to obtain treaty benefits and refundable SR&ED credits while the actual business is operated abroad; or failing to register as a money services business where the entity deals in virtual currency as a business in Canada
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR denial under ITA s.245 recharacterizing the arrangement, disallowing deductions and treaty benefits; sham doctrine reassessments; administrative monetary penalties under the PCMLTFA up to CAD 500,000 for a non-registered money services business dealing in virtual currency; potential strike-off under the BC Business Corporations Act for abandonment; Criminal Code laundering charges carrying up to ten years imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a sham or shell corporation risk veil-piercing where the corporation acts as a mere agent of a foreign principal, personal liability for corporate income tax and GST/HST under ITA s.227.1, statutory liability under the BC Business Corporations Act for false corporate records, and personal AML penalties where compliance functions were under their control; egregious cases support director disqualification orders and travel watch-listing where outstanding criminal warrants are issued for evasion or money laundering
